title: The French president is elected for five years and may not serve more than two consecutive terms
summary: The French president is elected for five years and may not serve more than two consecutive terms.
body: Article 6 says the president is elected for five years by direct universal suffrage, and that no one may hold office for more than two consecutive terms. The source says: "Head of state selection , Head of state term length , Claim of universal suffrage The President of the Republic shall be elected for a term of five years by direct universal suffrage." The consecutive-term limit is in the article. The mode of the election is left in part to an organic law, as the article also says.
